Executive Order 11135
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE EASTERN, WESTERN  
AND SOUTHEASTERN CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE COMMITTEES, AND  
CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers’ Conference Committees, 
designated in List A  attached hereto and made a part hereof, and 
certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad 
Signalmen, a labor organization; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NO W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (4:5 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create; a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern 
Carriers’ Conference Committees, or by their employees, in the condi­
tions out of which the disputes arose.

record.reasoning: The held text hashes and cited quotes match, and EO 12553 expressly includes EO 11135. The revoking order is dated and signed February 25, 1986, with no later effective-date provision; March 3 is the Federal Register publication date. The claim puts March 3 in both end-date fields while its own mechanism and judgment reason say the revocation took effect February 25. The board report date is unheld, so the evidence does not establish a precise earlier performance end; that gap does not cure the false formal end date.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11135 (signed 1964-01-03, 29 FR 125), read in full from the held official FR text layer (29 FR 125, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11135.txt offsets 542-2300; the representation is the official FR page OCR, location_verified false, page check not required by the record). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The order creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the disputes between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (List A) and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen ('I hereby create; a board of three members', offset 1559 onward), directs it to report 'within thirty days from the date o f this order' (offset 1798 onward) and recites the section 10 status quo (offset 2075 onward). The carrier list (List A) after the signature is an attached schedule identifying the parties, not a separate command. Deciding source: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt), whose operative sentence (offsets 691-966) revokes 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto', and whose table names this order ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes', offsets 19627-19699); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1986-02-25. The dossier lists 'target provision not located: EO:12553' because the machine scanner found no ACT record; I located the naming entry myself ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes' at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt offsets 19627-19699, inside the table introduced by the operative sentence at 691-966), so the end cites the held EO 12553 text as a whole (ACTOR_TEXT) with those offsets named here. Report-deadline ruling (2026-10-21, option C) applied: the report deadline (1964-02-02 (signing date 1964-01-03 plus 30 days; counting convention not ruled)) and the report itself are spent facts, not ends. The board's actual report (its date, and so the end of the 30-day status quo) is not held in the repository (no NMB report text under jobs/source-ladder/output/texts; no FETCH_QUEUE line yet), so the 'functionally spent' date is disclosed as unknown; under the report-deadline ruling it is not an end and does not change the first end. D6 / later events: the dossier chain and actor provisions show only EO 12553; the draft's later-event and whole-order-end proposals (OFR disposition note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986' and the 1989 Codification table 'Revoked by EO 12553') point to the same instrument and are attached as the end itself; a by-number scan of all held FR order texts and APP texts found no other naming instrument (EO_10298 and EO_10299 (16 FR 11135 page number), EO_11912 (FR Doc. 76-11135), EO_12553 (the revocation)). Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR or text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. No conflicts are listed in the draft or dossier. Machine searches pasted after review: OFR catalog (1937 onward; covers this order), U.S. Code and eCFR (0 hits for this order: no current-law citation). Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15): heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966, the 'No. Subject' table and the signature block were read; a word search of the whole held text for saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that and effective finds no savings, exception, pending-matter or transfer wording (the only 'effective' hit, line 597, is the subject column of another row). Own-residual check, reading EO 11135 in full (29 FR 125, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11135.txt offsets 542-2300): it created an ad hoc fact-finding board for one labor dispute and set its report duty; it created no office, fund, property or private right that could outlast the board, and any status-quo obligation was the statute's own and long spent. EO 12553 has no savings clause, and nothing of the order outlives its revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts in jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts (every hit read in context: EO_10298 and EO_10299 (16 FR 11135 page number), EO_11912 (FR Doc. 76-11135), EO_12553 (the revocation)); a by-number scan of the held American Presidency Project order texts (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts: no other order names it); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986): 'it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' (held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, offsets 691-966), followed by the table entry '11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes' (offsets 19627-19699). EO 12553 states no effective date (no 'effective', 'take effect', savings or exception wording in the held text), so the revocation took effect on signing, 1986-02-25.
